name: Object Animation
visualIdentity: Everyday objects support the subject through incremental movement, rotation, arrangement, and replacement. Preserve their real materials, scale, lighting, and contact shadows. The reference is supplemental, not a canonical source-collection style; distinguish photographed animation from digital simulation.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to playful product moments. The metadata also suggests hybrids for data explainers using objects as consistent units, and music-led promos with moves scheduled to verified beats. Broader product, editorial, explanatory, and illustrated narratives are listed as suitable; fit depends on subject and assets.
limitations: Avoid unrelated simultaneous movement, invented or misleading data scales, and lighting flicker. Preserve holds for comparisons and section changes. Camera orbit is only a possible motion reference: it needs real 3D depth or labeled parallax, or omit it. Do not use chapter transitions when they obscure causality or break a continuous shot or loop.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. Preserve actual object and asset colors, task or brand colors, and their semantic roles. Optional presentation-only fallback tokens are background #F1E9DD, foreground #3B423E, accent #8D8977; the accent is decorative, not normal text backing. No gradient. Check contrast in the composited scene; never recolor objects to meet it.
motionAndInteraction: Photograph incremental poses with fixed camera and lighting; preserve planned pose exposure and held states, without automatic in-betweening. Digital simulation is allowed only if labeled. For video, derive state from seekable composition time and verify direct and reverse seeks. Interactive HTML may use finite scroll progress for narrative states or beat-table playback with pause/mute; backward progress must restore states deterministically. Pointer orbit is optional and requires actual 3D depth, bounded camera movement, keyboard/touch support, and reduced-motion state.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is required. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied audio choices. For beat-led work, sync to verified beats, avoid drift, and leave room for comprehension. Check speech clarity, balance, clipping, and picture sync.
assetRequirements: Prepare photographed layers or numbered frames with transparency, consistent dimensions, clear names, and inspectable assets. Keep camera and lighting fixed. Pillow may crop and normalize frames; Python may manage preprocessing, while FFmpeg can encode image sequences and combine audio. These are suggested tools, not evidence of the original production method.
combinations: For data explainers, pair with style-097: each object represents one verified unit, with labels, honest scale, held comparisons, and an HTML text-table equivalent plus alt text. For product promos or social loops, pair with style-105: choreograph relational moves to verified beats, with section holds and fixed lighting. Preserve real object colors in both.
productionApproach: Select the visual renderer and motion method for fidelity and action first; the metadata lists no dedicated object renderer. Use HyperFrames for composition, seekable timing, synchronization, validation, and export. Remotion is only a documented fallback when HyperFrames is unavailable or verified to lack a required capability. Keep specialist rendering and motion separate from the pipeline; inspect representative frames and the decoded full video. Interactive HTML may use scroll or controls; those live inputs must not drive video export.
